pages.title: Making water safe
pages.description: Identify the hazard and follow the supplier notice before treating water.

pages.title: Finding emergency water
pages.description: Work from known potable supplies towards sources that need treatment.

pages.title: Boiling water
pages.description: Use heat to deal with germs when local notices permit boiling.

pages.title: Water filters and their limits
pages.description: Read the device rating before relying on a portable filter.

pages.title: Chemical disinfection
pages.description: Use a product labelled for treating drinking water and keep the instructions with it.

pages.title: Storing drinking water
pages.description: Build a reserve before you need it and keep it separate from utility water.

pages.title: Collecting rainwater
pages.description: Treat collected rain as a separate supply with contamination risks.

pages.title: Recognising and managing dehydration
pages.description: Start replacing fluid early while the person can drink safely.

pages.title: Household emergency kit
pages.description: Keep essential supplies together where everyone can find them.

pages.title: Household emergency plan
pages.description: Agree how to contact each other and where to meet.

pages.title: During a power cut
pages.description: Check whether neighbours are affected and report the fault.

pages.title: Preparing for flooding
pages.description: Move people to safety early and keep your route clear of floodwater.

pages.title: Assessing an emergency
pages.description: Treat threats to life before making a detailed assessment.

pages.title: Adult CPR and defibrillator
pages.description: Unresponsive and not breathing normally, or only gasping: call 999 and start CPR.

pages.title: Child and baby CPR
pages.description: A child or baby who is unresponsive and not breathing normally needs immediate CPR.

pages.title: Controlling severe bleeding
pages.description: Apply direct pressure immediately and get help.

pages.title: Cooling and covering burns
pages.description: Stop the burning and cool the affected skin as soon as possible.

pages.title: Choking: adults and children
pages.description: Call 999 as soon as you recognise choking; use speaker if alone.

pages.title: Choking: baby under one
pages.description: Call 999 on speaker and act immediately if the baby cannot cough, cry or breathe effectively.

pages.title: Hypothermia first aid
pages.description: Treat confusion, drowsiness or slurred speech after cold exposure as urgent.

pages.title: Recognising and treating heat illness
pages.description: Confusion, collapse or seizures in the heat can mean heatstroke.

pages.title: Supporting a suspected fracture
pages.description: Support the injured part in the position found and avoid further movement.

pages.title: Cleaning and dressing a minor wound
pages.description: Only clean a minor wound after bleeding is controlled.

pages.title: First aid supplies
pages.description: Keep a first aid kit accessible, dry and easy to take with you.

pages.title: Staying warm through a long heating outage
pages.description: Choose a dry occupied room and reduce avoidable heat loss.

pages.title: Preventing hypothermia
pages.description: Intervene while people can still walk, talk and change clothing normally.

pages.title: Emergency outdoor shelter
pages.description: Get away from immediate hazards, take shelter and call for help early.

pages.title: Lighting a fire outdoors
pages.description: Avoid lighting a fire when there is wildfire risk or local rules prohibit it.

pages.title: Fire in your home
pages.description: Warn others. If you can escape safely, get out, stay out and call 999.

pages.title: Carbon monoxide poisoning
pages.description: If you suspect carbon monoxide, get outside into fresh air immediately.

pages.title: Keeping heat in safely
pages.description: Reduce draughts and use dry layers, while keeping essential ventilation clear.

pages.title: Staying safe in extreme heat
pages.description: Move to a cooler place, drink regularly and watch for signs of heat illness.

pages.title: Smoke, heat and CO alarms
pages.description: Working alarms give early warning. Test them regularly and keep exits clear.

pages.title: Tent and camping fire safety
pages.description: Keep stoves, heaters, barbecues and flames out of tents and enclosed shelters.

pages.title: Wildfire safety
pages.description: If you see an uncontrolled outdoor fire, move away and call 999.

pages.title: Getting emergency help
pages.description: For immediate danger call 999 or 112 and ask for the emergency service you need.

pages.title: Reticulum basics
pages.description: Reticulum is a networking system that can operate over several kinds of connection.

pages.title: Nomad Network basics
pages.description: Nomad Network lets a node host small pages that other reachable nodes can read.

pages.title: LoRa basics
pages.description: LoRa is a low-power radio method; compatible settings and software are needed at both ends.

pages.title: How network relays work
pages.description: A relay can extend reach only if it is compatible, powered and able to hear both sides.

pages.title: Communicating without internet
pages.description: Agree a primary and backup method with people before an outage.

pages.title: Passing an emergency message by radio
pages.description: Write the message before transmitting and verify that someone received it.

pages.title: Understanding radio signal
pages.description: A received signal reading is a clue, not a delivery guarantee.

pages.title: Positioning a radio antenna
pages.description: A clear, safely positioned antenna can improve a link; test both directions.

pages.title: Making radio batteries last
pages.description: Schedule transmissions while keeping an agreed way to receive replies.

pages.title: Practising an emergency communications plan
pages.description: Agree who listens, when they listen and what they do after silence.

pages.title: UK radio rules
pages.description: Before transmitting, check the conditions that apply to your exact equipment, frequency and use.

pages.title: Preparing for a power cut
pages.description: Keep a torch, charged phone, power bank and written emergency numbers within reach.

pages.title: Battery capacity and power
pages.description: Watt-hours describe stored energy; watts describe the rate at which a device uses it.

pages.title: Estimating battery runtime
pages.description: Estimate runtime using usable watt-hours divided by the device’s average watts.

pages.title: Using a portable power station
pages.description: Test a portable station with its intended loads before depending on it.

pages.title: Charging from portable solar
pages.description: Match the array and cable to the station's labelled input limits.

pages.title: Home solar during a power cut
pages.description: Do not assume rooftop solar will power your home when the grid fails.

pages.title: Prioritising electrical loads
pages.description: List essential loads and estimate both their energy use and peak power.

pages.title: Charging and storing batteries
pages.description: Use the manufacturer’s charger or an approved compatible replacement.

pages.title: Using a fuel generator safely
pages.description: Operate outdoors in open air. Carbon monoxide can kill without warning.

pages.title: Electrical danger during an outage
pages.description: Keep clear of fallen power lines: assume they are live.

pages.title: Power for medical equipment
pages.description: If loss of power puts someone in immediate danger, call 999.

pages.title: Storing food without refrigeration
pages.description: Make the main reserve out of foods labelled for ambient storage.

pages.title: Food safety during a power cut
pages.description: Keep the doors shut and note when the power went off.

pages.title: Cooking without mains power
pages.description: Choose a cooking method based on available safe water, fuel and ventilation.

pages.title: Using a camping stove safely
pages.description: Check the fuel connection and outdoor site before lighting.

pages.title: Choosing a safe preservation method
pages.description: Pick a tested method you can complete with the equipment and controls you have.

pages.title: Planning meals from a limited reserve
pages.description: Build a use order from what is safe, what needs fuel and who needs it.

pages.title: Keeping food preparation clean
pages.description: Set up separate dirty and clean areas before opening food.

pages.title: Emergency sanitation
pages.description: If water or sewage services fail, follow the water company and local authority instructions.

pages.title: Emergency evacuation
pages.description: Leave promptly when instructed or when staying places you in immediate danger.

pages.title: Preparing for a severe storm
pages.description: Check warnings, secure loose items before weather worsens and stay away from hazards.

pages.title: Reading a map
pages.description: Identify scale, north and recognisable features before moving.

pages.title: Taking a compass bearing
pages.description: Use a baseplate compass to transfer a direction from a map.

pages.title: Navigating without GPS
pages.description: Use a paper map, compass and frequent position checks.

pages.title: Planning a safe walking route
pages.description: Write an offline route card before committing to exposed terrain.

pages.title: Signalling for help outdoors
pages.description: Choose a signal rescuers can detect from your safe position.

pages.title: What to do when lost
pages.description: Stop somewhere safe and keep the group together.

pages.title: Starting a small reliable food garden
pages.description: Start at a scale you can water and maintain.

pages.title: Running separate potable and utility supplies
pages.description: Use two sets of containers and track both reserves.

pages.title: Maintaining a working stock of supplies
pages.description: Record how much you can use before the next safe resupply.

pages.title: Maintaining essential equipment
pages.description: Test the equipment in the state it will be used, including spares.

pages.title: Wells and boreholes after flooding
pages.description: Switch to confirmed safe water if a private supply is flooded or treatment fails.

pages.title: Unsafe water quick card
pages.description: Use confirmed safe water for drinking, food and teeth.

pages.title: Flood quick card
pages.description: Get to higher ground by a dry route.

pages.title: Hypothermia quick card
pages.description: Suspect hypothermia? Call emergency services (UK: 999).

pages.title: Falling into cold water
pages.description: Float first and let your breathing settle before trying to swim.

pages.title: Collecting water from streams and lakes
pages.description: Carry a raw-water scoop, a marked raw container and a separate clean bottle.

pages.title: Settling and straining raw water
pages.description: Remove suspended dirt before treating water for germs.

pages.title: Water collection in freezing conditions
pages.description: Plan for frozen bottles, extra fuel and longer treatment times.

pages.title: Managing a limited water supply
pages.description: Track safe water and reduce avoidable uses before the reserve runs low.

pages.title: Choosing a safe fire site
pages.description: Use a fire only where you have permission, conditions are suitable and you can extinguish it.

pages.title: Preparing tinder and kindling
pages.description: Prepare all fuel sizes before striking a match at a permitted site.

pages.title: Selecting and sorting firewood
pages.description: Use approved supplied fuel first. Gather small dead fallen wood only where permitted.

pages.title: Lighting with matches or a lighter
pages.description: Light only a small prepared fire at a permitted site.

pages.title: Using a ferrocerium rod
pages.description: Practise spark ignition at a permitted fire site with water ready.

pages.title: Cooking heat in wet weather
pages.description: Choose a cold meal first if you cannot maintain safe heat outdoors.

pages.title: Maintaining a small cooking fire
pages.description: Maintain controllable heat for a pot rather than building a large flame.

pages.title: Extinguishing a campfire
pages.description: Leave enough water and time to cool every ember.

pages.title: Finding a safe shelter site
pages.description: Check hazards above, below and uphill before unloading.

pages.title: Pitching an A-frame tarp
pages.description: Use an A-frame for rain protection when you have secure supports and enough room.

pages.title: Pitching a tarp lean-to
pages.description: Use a sloping tarp for short-term shelter where wind direction is steady.

pages.title: Low shelter with natural insulation
pages.description: Use dry loose debris as supplementary insulation where collection is allowed.

pages.title: Insulating yourself from the ground
pages.description: Build the layer beneath you before adding more blankets above.

pages.title: Managing wind and rain in shelter
pages.description: Recheck the pitch once wind and rain start.

pages.title: Shelter construction hazards
pages.description: Reject any build with uncertain structure, ventilation or escape.

pages.title: Reading a UK grid reference
pages.description: Use the British National Grid letters plus eastings then northings.

pages.title: Following a bearing on foot
pages.description: Break a bearing into short safe legs between identifiable points.

pages.title: Reading terrain from contours
pages.description: Read the pattern of contours, then verify it on the ground.

pages.title: Cooking with limited fuel
pages.description: Choose meals that stay safe if the fuel supply runs out.

pages.title: Deciding when food must be discarded
pages.description: Use storage history and packaging condition to decide what to keep.

pages.title: Avoiding poisoning when foraging
pages.description: Use known safe food when identification, permission or site history is uncertain.

pages.title: Preparing a meal outdoors
pages.description: Use a stable setup and choose a meal you can cook and serve in one session.

pages.title: Setting up an emergency toilet
pages.description: Switch to containment if the sewer or septic system cannot safely take flushes.

pages.title: Containing and disposing of human waste
pages.description: Set up a route for waste before relying on a temporary toilet.

pages.title: Handwashing with a small water supply
pages.description: Provide flowing safe water from a tap container or a helper pouring a jug.

pages.title: Personal hygiene without running water
pages.description: Use small batches of safe water and keep used water out of the clean container.

pages.title: Handling contaminated clothing and equipment
pages.description: Separate soiled items at the point of use and handle them as little as possible.

pages.title: Keeping a temporary camp sanitary
pages.description: Separate the clean water and cooking area from toilets, waste and laundry.

pages.title: Managing solid waste and wash water
pages.description: Plan how to remove waste before it attracts animals or reaches water.

pages.title: Recognising circulatory shock
pages.description: Treat shock as life-threatening, especially after serious bleeding or injury.

pages.title: Spotting a worsening wound
pages.description: Check wounds again during a prolonged wait for care.

pages.title: Deciding whether to move a casualty
pages.description: Weigh immediate danger against the risk of moving an injured person.

pages.title: Monitoring someone awaiting care
pages.description: Record changes and restart the emergency assessment whenever the person deteriorates.

pages.title: Severe bleeding quick card
pages.description: Press firmly and continuously. Call emergency services (UK: 999).

pages.title: Heat illness quick card
pages.description: Move to shade, remove excess clothes, cool with water and fan.

pages.title: Making a visible rescue signal
pages.description: Use contrast by day and a controlled light signal at night.

pages.title: Morse timing and the SOS signal
pages.description: Use distinct short and long pulses that can be recognised at a distance.

pages.title: Communicating your location
pages.description: Write a position that can be read back without your map or phone.

pages.title: Distress signalling quick card
pages.description: Stay somewhere safe and tell rescuers your location when possible.

pages.title: Setting up a non-potable rainwater store
pages.description: Use a covered water butt for suitable non-drinking jobs.

pages.title: Saving seed for the next growing season
pages.description: Start with a healthy familiar crop and a variety likely to breed true.

pages.title: Temporary repairs to fabric and gear
pages.description: Repair low-consequence damage first, such as a torn bag or tarp.

pages.title: Managing a prolonged infrastructure outage
pages.description: Reassess people, shelter, safe water and communications before each new work period.

pages.title: Preparing a small outdoor fire
pages.description: Plan the entire burn, including putting it out, before lighting.

pages.title: Making decisions when stranded
pages.description: Pause, get everyone safe, and choose the next action from what you can verify.

pages.title: Settling raw water quick card
pages.description: Settle muddy water in a marked raw container.

pages.title: Campfire extinguishing quick card
pages.description: Stop adding fuel early. Keep enough water to put it out.

pages.title: Tarp shelter quick card
pages.description: Choose safe drained ground clear of falling branches, flood routes and rockfall.

pages.title: UK grid reference quick card
pages.description: British National Grid: use the square letters, then read right and up.

pages.title: Emergency toilet quick card
pages.description: If told not to flush, contain the waste.

pages.title: Rescue message quick card
pages.description: Send location and format, incident, number of people, dangers and needed help.

pages.title: Portable solar input quick card
pages.description: Confirm input voltage, current, power, polarity and connectors before connecting.
